items.title: Amazon CloudFront now supports AWS Lambda Web Functions as an origin
items.blurb: Starting today, you can deliver web applications built on AWS Lambda Web Functions through CloudFront's global edge network.

items.title: AWS Security Hub now supports resource criticality for prioritization
items.blurb: Today, AWS Security Hub adds resource criticality to exposure prioritization, helping central security teams focus on the exposures that threaten their most business-critical resources.

items.title: Plasma 6.8 released (KDE's 30th birthday)
items.blurb: KDE’s 30th anniversary is an opportunity to look forward: Plasma 6.8 helps lay the foundation for the future of Plasma and free desktops.

items.title: Amazon ECS adds LiveTaskCount and removes the charge for RunningTaskCount metric
items.blurb: Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) announces LiveTaskCount, a new ECS service metric that reports how many tasks are actively running in your service, available to all customers at no additional charge.

items.title: AWS Agent Registry now supports custom metadata for registry records
items.blurb: AWS Agent Registry is the centralized, governed catalog for agents, MCP servers, agent skills, gateways, and custom resources within your organization.

items.title: Amazon DCV releases version 2026.0 with RHEL 10 support and new clients
items.blurb: Amazon DCV 2026.0 is now available, adding support for RHEL 10, Rocky Linux 10, CentOS 10, and Ubuntu 26.04 along with a new macOS client and updated Windows and Linux clients.

items.title: AWS Deadline Cloud now helps users find their accessible resources in the Deadline Cloud monitor
items.blurb: AWS Deadline Cloud now lets users who have access to specific queues, fleets, or jobs, rather than an entire farm, find the resources they can reach directly from the Deadline Cloud monitor.

items.title: Backstage 1.55 Adds Scaffolder Task Recovery and Removes Deprecated Catalog APIs
items.blurb: Backstage 1.55 adds opt-in recovery for Software Template tasks, resuming crashed or timed-out runs from the last completed step.
